quests.instruction: Add s to “cat”. How does the ending sound?
quests.hint: Say cats slowly and listen to the last sound.
quests.explanation: In “cats”, the s says /s/ because the sound before it, /t/, is quiet.

quests.instruction: “Dogs” has an ending too. What sound does the s make this time?
quests.hint: Say dogs and put your fingers on your throat at the end.
quests.explanation: In “dogs”, the s says /z/ because the sound before it, /g/, uses your voice.
quests.funFact: The ending s can say /s/ or /z/. It copies the sound before it: quiet sounds are followed by /s/ and buzzing sounds by /z/.

quests.instruction: Which word has an s ending that sounds like /z/?
quests.hint: Listen for a buzz at the end.
quests.explanation: “Beds” ends with /z/ because /d/ is a buzzing sound. “Cats” and “hats” end with /s/.

quests.instruction: When a word ends in s, x, sh, ch or z, we add es. Which word means more than one box?
quests.hint: Say the word. You can hear an extra syllable.
quests.explanation: “Boxes” adds es because the word ends in x. You hear an extra syllable, /iz/.
quests.funFact: Dishes, boxes and buses each have an extra syllable when you say them.

quests.instruction: How does the ending of “buses” sound?
quests.hint: Count the syllables in buses.
quests.explanation: “Buses” has two syllables, and the ending sounds like /iz/.

quests.instruction: Which word needs es to mean more than one?
quests.hint: Look at the last letters. Which word ends in sh?
quests.explanation: “Dish” ends with sh, so we add es to make “dishes”. “Cup” and “pen” just add s.

quests.instruction: The ending -ed can say /t/. Which word has that ending sound?
quests.hint: Listen to the very last sound of each word. One is a quiet tap.
quests.explanation: In “jumped”, -ed says /t/. “Played” ends with /d/ and “wanted” ends with /id/.
quests.funFact: The ending -ed is always spelled the same way, but it can be said three ways: /t/, /d/ or /id/.

quests.instruction: Which word has the -ed ending that says /d/?
quests.hint: Listen for a buzzing sound at the end.
quests.explanation: “Played” ends with /d/ because the /ay/ before it uses your voice.

quests.instruction: Which word has -ed saying /id/, which adds a whole extra syllable?
quests.hint: Count the syllables in each word.
quests.explanation: “Wanted” has two syllables because -ed says /id/ after a /t/ sound. “Hugged” and “helped” each have one syllable.
quests.funFact: After /t/ or /d/, -ed says /id/ and adds an extra syllable, as in wanted and needed.

quests.instruction: How many syllables are in “jumped”?
quests.hint: Clap as you say jumped.
quests.explanation: “Jumped” has just 1 syllable because the -ed says /t/.
quests.funFact: Jumped has one syllable, but wanted has two.

quests.instruction: Now try “wanted”. How many syllables does it have?
quests.hint: Clap the beats. Does the ending add a beat?
quests.explanation: “Wanted” has 2 syllables: want-ed. The -ed says /id/.

quests.instruction: Which word has -ed saying /t/?
quests.hint: Listen to the last sound of each word.
quests.explanation: “Stopped” ends with /t/. “Hunted” ends with /id/ and “planned” ends with /d/.

quests.instruction: Add -ing to “jump”. Which word do you make?
quests.hint: Just add the ending to the end of the word.
quests.explanation: “Jump” plus -ing makes “jumping”. No letters change.
quests.funFact: Adding -ing does not change how the base word sounds: jump, jumping.

quests.instruction: Add -ing to “run”. We double the n. Which word is correct?
quests.hint: After a short vowel and one consonant, the consonant usually doubles.
quests.explanation: “Run” has a short vowel and one consonant at the end, so we double the n: running.

quests.instruction: Add -ing to “make”. We drop the silent e. Which word is correct?
quests.hint: The silent e is not needed when -ing starts with a vowel.
quests.explanation: “Make” drops its silent e, then adds -ing: making. The a still says long a.

quests.instruction: “Hoping” and “hopping” sound different. Which one has a long o?
quests.hint: Listen to the vowel in each word. One has a long vowel.
quests.explanation: “Hoping” comes from hope, so the o stays long. “Hopping” comes from hop, so the o stays short.
quests.funFact: The doubled consonant in hopping tells you the vowel is short.

quests.instruction: Which word has a short a?
quests.hint: Look for the doubled consonant.
quests.explanation: “Tapping” has a doubled p, so the a is short. “Taping” and “tape” have long a.

quests.instruction: Which is spelled correctly?
quests.hint: Think about the vowel in “stop”. Is it short or long?
quests.explanation: “Stop” has a short o, so we double the p: stopping.

quests.instruction: Add -er to “fast” to mean “more fast”. Which word do you make?
quests.hint: The ending -er compares two things.
quests.explanation: “Fast” plus -er makes “faster”, which compares two things.
quests.funFact: Adding -er can make a word compare things, as in fast and faster.

quests.instruction: Which word means “a person who teaches”?
quests.hint: Look for the ending that names a person.
quests.explanation: “Teacher” adds -er to “teach” to name the person who does it. The /er/ sound is the same.

quests.instruction: Add -er to “big”. We double the g. Which word is correct?
quests.hint: Big has a short vowel and one consonant at the end.
quests.explanation: “Big” has a short i and ends in one consonant, so we double the g: bigger.

quests.instruction: Which word means “most tall”?
quests.hint: Look for the ending that means “the most”.
quests.explanation: “Tallest” adds -est to “tall”, and it means the most tall.
quests.funFact: Adding -est means “the most”. Tall, taller and tallest show how a word grows.

quests.instruction: Add -est to “hot”. Which word is correct?
quests.hint: Hot has a short vowel and one consonant at the end.
quests.explanation: “Hot” has a short o and one final consonant, so we double the t: hottest.

quests.instruction: Add -est to “nice”. We drop the silent e first. Which word is correct?
quests.hint: The silent e is not needed when the ending starts with a vowel.
quests.explanation: “Nice” drops its silent e before -est, so it becomes “nicest”. The i still says long i.
quests.funFact: Words like nicer, nicest and nicely show how one base word grows with new endings.

quests.instruction: Which word ends with /iz/?
quests.hint: Listen for an extra syllable at the end.
quests.explanation: “Wishes” adds es and an extra syllable, /iz/. “Wished” ends with /t/ and “wishing” ends with -ing.
quests.funFact: Wish, wishes, wished and wishing are one base word with different endings.

quests.instruction: Which word has 2 syllables?
quests.hint: Clap each word. Which one has two beats?
quests.explanation: “Jumping” has 2 syllables: jump-ing. “Jumped” and “jumps” each have one.

quests.instruction: Which word is made from the base word “help”?
quests.hint: Look for the base word inside the new word.
quests.explanation: “Helping” is help + ing. “Hoping” comes from hope.

quests.instruction: Which word has an ending that says /t/?
quests.hint: Listen for the quick tap at the end.
quests.explanation: “Walked” ends with /t/. “Called” ends with /d/ and “needed” ends with /id/.
quests.funFact: Walked, jumped and helped all end with /t/ even though they are spelled with -ed.

quests.instruction: Which word is spelled correctly? “He is ___ the ball.”
quests.hint: Add -ing to kick. Does the word need any change?
quests.explanation: “Kick” ends in ck, so we simply add -ing: kicking.

quests.instruction: Which word has /z/ at the end?
quests.hint: Listen for a buzzing sound.
quests.explanation: “Dogs” ends with /z/. “Cats” ends with /s/ and “boxes” ends with /iz/.
